$comment: Platform-level tool isolation for this project.
These deny rules aim to make Robinhood order-placement tools unavailable during
normal research sessions, so that 'the agent does not place orders' is enforced by
the harness and not only by this repository's own code.
VERIFY THIS YOURSELF with /permissions before relying on it. Deny rules are
documented to take precedence over allow rules, but the exact matcher behaviour
for MCP tool names should be confirmed in your Claude Code version rather than
assumed. Treat this file as defence in depth, never as the primary control:
the primary controls are execution_mode=DRY_RUN, agent_enabled=false, and the
absence of any order-submission code path in src/.
The PreToolUse hook below confines an UNATTENDED SCHEDULED RUN's writes to
reports/, research/ and the scheduled log files. It enforces only while
RH_AGENT_SCHEDULED_RUN=1 is set, which scripts/scheduled_evaluation.sh sets and
an interactive session does not, so ordinary development here is unaffected.
A path specifier on a file tool (--allowedTools 'Write(reports/**)') was tested
against Claude Code 2.1.263 and matches NOTHING -- it denied writes to the very
directory it named, while bare 'Write' allowed them everywhere. The hook is
therefore what actually scopes the writes; postflight also fingerprints the whole
repository tree, so an out-of-scope write is reported even if the hook is bypassed.
NOT denied here: the promotion script and the history-ingest script. Both must
be unavailable to an UNATTENDED run and available to a human (and to an
interactive session helping one) -- a distinction this file cannot express,
since its rules apply to every session in the repository equally. The controls
that CAN express it are used instead: each script refuses outright when
RH_AGENT_SCHEDULED_RUN=1; both are listed in src/scheduling.FORBIDDEN_SCRIPTS so
the runners are tested never to invoke them; and a scheduled run is granted at
most two exact Bash commands anyway (check_status.py and validate_plan.py), so
it cannot reach either script.
approve_decision.py IS denied here, and the asymmetry is deliberate: approval is
a human act in every session (CLAUDE.md 0a), whereas minting a PROPOSED decision
is already within an interactive evaluation's normal authority -- validate_decision.py
--log does exactly that and is not denied.
close_stale_decision.py is denied for the same reason. Closing a stale decision out
releases part of the month's authorization back to the budget and writes
state/executions.json, so it moves the pipeline exactly as approval does -- in the
other direction, but by the same hand. It is a human act in every session, and the
model has no business performing it however obviously correct the closure looks.
The script ALSO refuses when RH_AGENT_SCHEDULED_RUN=1 or RH_AGENT_SCHEDULED_POST_RUN=1,
and is listed in src/scheduling.FORBIDDEN_SCRIPTS, so an unattended run cannot reach
it by any route. None of this touches a human typing the command in their own
terminal: these rules bind Claude's Bash tool, not the shell.
